summary: 12870b8fde's narrow-format refusal is placed in the LEAF (perform_blit(), blit.c:102) rather than at the entry function, so it returns after pgraph_vk_image_blit() has already committed destination-surface bookkeeping for a write that will not happen, and before three memory_region_set_client_dirty() calls that advertise it. For a blit whose rect covers the whole destination surface, blit.c:570-571 clear surf_dest->download_pending and surf_dest->draw_dirty on the grounds that 'the blit will completely replace the surface', and blit.c:573 sets upload_pending; perform_blit() then declines and writes nothing, so GPU-rendered content is discarded and the VkImage is reloaded from VRAM the blit never touched. The cited precedent pgraph_vk_solid_line() puts its identical bytes_per_pixel != 4 guard at blit.c:782, at the TOP of the entry function, above every soft guard and before any state is mutated. The commit copies solid_line's warn-once idiom but not its placement. This is NOT the old overrun and NOT memory unsafety -- the refusal removes the out-of-bounds write and does not reintroduce it; it is a different wrongness in the same path.
scenario: A guest binds an NV062 context-surfaces-2D pair with SET_COLOR_FORMAT = LE_R5G6B5 (or LE_Y8), sets NV09F_SET_OPERATION = BLEND_AND, and issues a blit whose rect covers the whole destination surface -- which is the `else` branch at blit.c:567, not an exotic case, since `adjusted_height >= surf_dest->height && row_pixels >= surf_dest->width` is exactly a full-surface blit. download_pending and draw_dirty are cleared, so anything the GPU had rendered into that surface and not yet written back is DISCARDED; upload_pending is set, so the image is reloaded from VRAM that perform_blit() then refuses to write; and the three memory_region_set_client_dirty() calls at blit.c:689, :691 and :699 tell DIRTY_MEMORY_VGA, DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A_TEX and DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A that the range changed when nothing did, invalidating texture bindings and forcing a redraw for no write. The difference from a correct skip is the difference between 'this blit did nothing' and 'this blit reset the destination to stale VRAM and told three subsystems it had written'. Unmeasurable on any fleet: all 20 ImgBlt_BLENDAND_* goldens are XRGB or ZRGB, both 32bpp, so no capture reaches bytes_per_pixel != 4 on this branch.
remediation: Hoist the decision into pgraph_vk_image_blit(), after the bytes_per_pixel switch and BEFORE the surf_dest block at blit.c:561: `if (image_blit->operation == NV09F_SET_OPERATION_BLEND_AND && bytes_per_pixel != 4) { warn once; return; }`. Keep the leaf guard as a defensive return so no future caller can reach the 32bpp indexing. That makes the refusal a genuine no-op rather than a partially-committed one, and it is the placement the cited precedent already uses 200 lines lower in the same file. A REMEDIATION IS A CLAIM: if the lane prefers the guard only in the leaf, the alternative is to skip the surf_dest mutations and the three dirty marks on the same condition, which is strictly more code in more places for the same effect -- declining with that reasoning logged is defensible, declining with no reasoning is not.
evidence: Guard at blit.c:102-114 inside perform_blit()'s BLEND_AND branch. Caller bookkeeping at blit.c:561-575 (surf_dest lookup, the partial/full branch, download_pending = false at :570, draw_dirty = false at :571, upload_pending = true at :573). perform_blit() is called at blit.c:589 and :612 and via perform_blit_tiled() at :582/:603. Unconditional dirty marks at blit.c:689 (DIRTY_MEMORY_VGA), :691 (DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A_TEX), :699 (DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A). Precedent placement: pgraph_vk_solid_line() at blit.c:730, its format switch at :763-780, its bytes_per_pixel != 4 warn-once return at :782-793, ABOVE its own soft guards at :795-800. GL's twin b9d845d316 has the same leaf placement, so this applies to both renderers. Class emptiness: `ls /home/justin/goldens/results/Image_blit | grep -c BLENDAND` -> 20, all ImgBlt_BLENDAND_XRGB_* or _ZRGB_*.

summary: Two of the nine must_not_move keys -- Color_Zeta_Disable/MaskOff_ZB and Null_surface/XemuBug893 -- are in suites that a per-suite arm will not contain, and request.sh's prediction gate cannot see it because it validates keys against the GOLDENS directory rather than against the requested suites. All 11 keys do have a capture on disk and not merely a golden (the OverlapFIFO check passes), but they are spread across THREE result directories, because the corpus sweep requests one suite per run. The prediction's own prose calls the arm 'a narrowed per-suite disc'. So the gate queues clean, the arm returns PRE-REGISTERED, and 2 of 11 legs bind to no row -- AGENTS.md's inert-prediction class 1 arriving through disc composition instead of through spelling, which is the only form the gate was built for. The two inert legs are not decoration: they are the regression guard on the other two suites that traverse the edited update_surface_part(), which is the main regression risk the prediction itself names.
scenario: The arm is queued the way every Color_zeta_overlap result on disk was queued -- dispatch/results/z-c866527e03-016-Color_zeta_overlap/request.json reads "suites": ["Color zeta overlap"]. ab_compare expands each must_not_move pattern with fnmatch against the captures the two arms actually scored, so Color_Zeta_Disable/MaskOff_ZB and Null_surface/XemuBug893 match nothing on either arm: they cannot pass and cannot fail. The verdict reads PRE-REGISTERED with 9 of 11 legs measured and nothing indicating which two were not. Because NV2A_UNIMPLEMENTED is a no-op in shipping builds (DEBUG_NV2A_FEATURES defaults to 0, debug.h:58-59, :77), the capture is the ONLY oracle for this policy change, so a leg that binds to no row leaves that half of the regression surface with no observable at all.
remediation: Queue the arm over all three suites: --suites "Color zeta overlap" "Color Zeta Disable" "Null surface" (index spellings verified against docs/testing/nv2a_index.json; the results-directory spellings the prediction keys use are Color_zeta_overlap, Color_Zeta_Disable, Null_surface). OR drop the two out-of-suite keys and state in the prediction why the guard is narrower than the stated risk. Either is acceptable; queuing one suite while carrying eleven keys is not. This is a defect in the verification apparatus and not in hw/, so it does not hold the code fold -- but it must be settled BEFORE the arm is queued, because a leg scored in neither arm cannot be recovered afterwards. Separately worth routing to lane.toolsmith: request.sh's gate builds its `known` set from $GOLDENS/<suite>/*.png (request.sh:299-305) and answers 'does a golden exist', not 'will this arm score it'; it could cross-check the prediction's keys against the request's own --suites list, which is information it already has at queue time.
evidence: Prediction must_not_move lists 7 Color_zeta_overlap keys plus Color_Zeta_Disable/MaskOff_ZB and Null_surface/XemuBug893; expect lists 2 more Color_zeta_overlap keys. Captures verified present on disk: all 9 Color_zeta_overlap in dispatch/results/z-c866527e03-016-Color_zeta_overlap/captures1/; Color_Zeta_Disable::MaskOff_ZB.png in .../z-c866527e03-013-Color_Zeta_Disable/captures1/; Null_surface::XemuBug893.png in .../z-after-048-Null_surface/captures1/ -- three separate result directories. Per-suite request shape: z-c866527e03-016-Color_zeta_overlap/request.json "suites": ["Color zeta overlap"], suites.txt one line. Gate scope: request.sh:299-305 builds `known` by listing $GOLDENS (default /home/justin/goldens/results) per suite directory; binds() at :313-314 is fnmatch against that set only; all 11 keys have goldens, so the gate passes. AGENTS.md, 'Three ways a prediction can be inert', class 1.

summary: a_ref (12870b8fde) and b_ref (e71a9952d1) are ancestors of the lane branch worktree-agent-aa4f3448ff981e82f and of NEITHER the campaign tip cce5eec199. That is correct today, while the commits are held, and it is what 'register last' asks for. It stops being correct the moment the fold cherry-picks: both shas are rewritten, and the binding then fails in the one direction AGENTS.md names as the dangerous one -- reachable from a live branch but not an ancestor of the branch under test -- so the dispatcher builds them successfully and produces a clean, confident measurement of the PRE-FOLD tree. Nothing errors and nothing warns at the moment the binding breaks.
scenario: The orchestrator cherry-picks 12870b8fde and e71a9952d1 onto cce5eec199, rewriting both shas. The device hold is later lifted and the #88 arm is queued against the registered prediction. request.sh records the prediction's sha256, which is unchanged; ab_compare resolves a_ref and b_ref, which are still reachable from the lane worktree's branch; dispatcher.sh builds them. Arm B is therefore the pre-fold e71a9952d1 -- without anything the fold changed, including any M1 remediation landed on top of it -- and the pair completes, scores, and reports PRE-REGISTERED. This exact failure hit #59 twice in one day, once from precisely this cause (a reachable-but-not-ancestor ref built successfully into an arm B missing the lane's later work).
remediation: The orchestrator re-registers the prediction with the folded shas immediately after the cherry-pick and before the arm is queued. Re-registering is cheap; a silently-wrong arm costs device time plus the time to discover it was void. Do NOT queue the arm against the pre-fold refs on the grounds that they still build -- that they still build is the defect, not the reassurance. Run merge-base --is-ancestor on BOTH refs after the last rebase, not before. Not in hw/; this is the orchestrator's action at fold time, and it is also the queue-time gate AGENTS.md recommends and that does not yet exist: a b_ref that is not an ancestor of the branch the arm is nominally testing should be refused at queue time.
evidence: merge-base --is-ancestor 12870b8fde worktree-agent-aa4f3448ff981e82f -> true; same for e71a9952d1. merge-base --is-ancestor 12870b8fde cce5eec199 -> false; same for e71a9952d1. Lane branch log: 201d158e72 (prediction) -> e71a9952d1 (#88) -> 12870b8fde (#84) -> 9ebb1c6d33. AGENTS.md, 'A prediction naming a b_ref must be registered AFTER the last rebase', and 'The reachable-but-not-an-ancestor case is the dangerous one, because it fails in the direction that looks like success.'

summary: 12870b8fde's commit message says "perform_blit()'s signature gained `unsigned int bytes_per_pixel` before `BetaState *beta`, and all four call sites pass it." There are THREE call sites, not four: blit.c:375 (from perform_blit_tiled), :589 (linear body) and :612 (leftover row). perform_blit_tiled()'s own two call sites at :582 and :603 already carried bytes_per_pixel and are unchanged by this commit. GL's twin b9d845d316 also touches three. No defect -- every actual call site passes the right value, and the clean build is the completeness proof -- but the count IS the enumeration this audit was dispatched to check, and the commit message is where this project keeps its reasoning, so a wrong count there is what the next reader trusts instead of re-deriving.
scenario: No failure scenario in the code. The failure is documentary: whoever re-queues the arm-B ref of blit38-blend-and-divide.json is told by this message that four call sites moved, and the coordination note in the same message is otherwise accurate and will be relied on. An off-by-one enumeration in a message whose whole purpose is to say exactly what moved underneath a held prediction is the kind of small wrongness that gets cited rather than checked. Downgraded to LOW for exactly that reason: it is an accuracy defect in a record, not in behaviour.
remediation: Amend the held commit's message to say three direct perform_blit() call sites plus two pre-existing perform_blit_tiled() sites, or note the correction in the fold commit. The commit is unfolded, so amending is free. Reviewed-and-not-fixed with the count recorded in this audit is an acceptable outcome under the LOW rule.
evidence: git grep -n perform_blit 12870b8fde -- hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/blit.c returns the definition at :34, comment references at :56 and :355, the perform_blit_tiled definition at :357, and calls at :375, :582 (tiled), :589, :603 (tiled), :612 -- three perform_blit() calls. git show b9d845d316 -- hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/gl/blit.c shows three added `bytes_per_pixel, beta);` argument lines. Android arm64 build of 201d158e72: BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 5m 12s, GRADLE_EXIT=0, zero error: lines -- for a signature change that is the structural proof no call site was missed.

summary: perform_blit_tiled() passes `chunk / bytes_per_pixel` as `width` and `chunk` as `width_bytes`, so at this one call site width * bytes_per_pixel does NOT equal width_bytes when chunk is not a multiple of bytes_per_pixel. SRCCOPY is unaffected because it memmoves width_bytes. For BLEND_AND at 32bpp the loop blends 4 * (chunk / 4) bytes while `done += chunk` advances the source by chunk, so chunk % 4 bytes per chunk are skipped and the source skews against the destination for the remainder of the row; a leading chunk of 1, 2 or 3 gives width == 0 and blends nothing. Pre-existing and untouched by this commit. Filed because the commit's central argument is that `width` counts destination-format pixels and the clamp is authoritative, and this is the one site where the byte count and the pixel count are not two views of the same number.
scenario: chunk = 16 - (offset % 16) at blit.c:370, and offset inherits context_surfaces->dest_offset, which pgraph.c:2024 stores as `parameter & 0x07FFFFFF` with NO alignment mask -- so an unaligned guest destination offset is reachable state. It additionally needs a valid GPU tile covering the destination AND a blit that overruns it (clipped_dest_size < dest_size at blit.c:547), which is why nothing has hit it: the tiled path is only taken for the overrun case, deliberately, per the investigation in docs/investigations/gpu-tile-blit-swizzle.md. The outcome is a wrong picture inside the tiled BLEND_AND rect, never an overrun: width can only shrink under truncation, so no extra byte is ever touched. No unsafety.
remediation: Cheapest: one sentence in the new comment naming blit.c:375 as the exception to `width_bytes == width * bytes_per_pixel`, so the authoritative-clamp argument is complete rather than almost complete. Stronger: align chunk down to a whole pixel (`chunk -= chunk % bytes_per_pixel`, with the remainder picked up by the next iteration) so the two counts agree at every site -- but that changes the tiled path's chunking for SRCCOPY too and wants its own arm, and BlitBeyondWidth is currently bit-exact, so it should not be bundled here. Reviewed-and-not-fixed with the reasoning logged is the expected outcome.
evidence: perform_blit_tiled() at blit.c:357-386; chunk computed at :370-373; the call at :375-379 passes `chunk / bytes_per_pixel, 1, chunk`. Guest offset unmasked for alignment: pgraph.c:2024 `context_surfaces_2d->dest_offset = parameter & 0x07FFFFFF`. Tiled path gated on clipped_dest_size < dest_size at blit.c:547 and dest_tile.valid at :580. patch_alpha_tiled() at blit.c:389 has the same shape with a hard-coded `width_pixels * 4` and is safe only because needs_alpha_patching is set for X8R8G8B8 and X8R8G8B8_Z8R8G8B8 alone, both 4bpp.

summary: The new early return is reachable on the DOWNLOAD path (upload == false), which GL's identical return cannot be, and on that path it skips the only site that clears pg->surface_zeta.draw_dirty and pg->surface_zeta.write_enabled_cache. This is the direct consequence of the asymmetry the commit correctly identifies: GL's gate is `upload && (buffer_dirty || mem_dirty || no_binding)`, so the no-binding disjunct is under `upload`; Vulkan's is `!current_binding || (upload && (buffer_dirty || mem_dirty))`, so with upload == false and zeta_binding == NULL the gate is satisfied by the first disjunct alone. The commit verified the gate is more permissive and concluded only the policy needed porting -- which is right about the gate -- but did not carry through that the extra permissiveness changes the reachability of its own new return.
scenario: Once zeta has declined, r->zeta_binding is NULL. pgraph_vk_set_surface_dirty() sets pg->surface_zeta.draw_dirty |= zeta at draw.c:6766 INDEPENDENTLY of whether r->zeta_binding exists, so the flag latches true on the next draw with zeta writes enabled, and write_enabled_cache with it. pgraph_vk_surface_update()'s non-upload branch then tests `(zeta_write || pg->surface_zeta.write_enabled_cache) && pg->surface_zeta.draw_dirty`, which is true on every non-upload update for as long as the overlap persists, so update_surface_part(d, false, false) is re-entered each time -- paying pgraph_vk_ensure_not_in_render_pass() and a pgraph_vk_surface_get() hash lookup -- to reach the same early return. DELIBERATELY DOWNGRADED, and here is what I could not establish: the sharper form of this finding is that when colour finally releases the address, the first non-upload update after zeta binds it carries a draw_dirty accumulated from draws in which zeta had no image, and so downloads a surface zeta never drew into. I traced it and could not make it wrong -- download_surface_deferred() guards on the BINDING's own draw_dirty and on download_generation == draw_generation (surface.c:1366-1372), and the image it would write is the one the guest did render at that address. So the failure scenario is a per-update hash lookup, not wrong pixels. The strong form has no failure scenario and is recorded as an opinion.
remediation: One line: clear pg_surface->draw_dirty and pg_surface->write_enabled_cache alongside buffer_dirty on the decline path, which keeps the Vulkan gate's extra permissiveness and makes the decline a complete 'request handled' the way the normal path's surface.c:3526/3547-3548 are. Alternative: gate the decline on `upload` so it mirrors GL exactly -- but that reintroduces the pre-change behaviour on the download path, which is worse (it creates a zeta image, evicts colour, and copies a never-rendered image back over VRAM), so prefer the first. THE LANE MAY REASONABLY DECLINE BOTH and log that the measured cost is a hash lookup with no defect behind it; that is an acceptable LOW outcome under the audit loop.
evidence: Early return at surface.c:3288-3289 (`pg_surface->buffer_dirty = false; return;`). Vulkan gate at surface.c:3213-3214. GL's fixed gate: `if (upload && (surface->buffer_dirty || mem_dirty || no_binding))` in fada1d89d4. The skipped tail at surface.c:3536-3549 is the only site clearing pg_surface->write_enabled_cache (:3547) and pg_surface->draw_dirty (:3548). pg->surface_zeta.draw_dirty set with no binding check at draw.c:6766; the per-binding flags at draw.c:6773/6782 ARE behind a binding check. Non-upload dispatch condition in pgraph_vk_surface_update(). download_surface_deferred() double guard at surface.c:1366-1372. unbind_surface() is NULL-safe at surface.c:1829-1845.
